data.title: U.S. Treasury Prices Rise as Steady 20-Year Auction Supports Longer-Dated Bonds
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. Treasury prices rose during Wednesday’s U.S. trading session, led by longer-dated bonds, as demand at a 20-year auction remained steady. The 2-year/10-year and 5-year/30-year spreads moved near their session lows. The auction’s yield was in line with pre-sale trading, extending the earlier flattening of the yield curve.

Most of the gains came during the U.S. morning, when Treasuries drew support after spot stocks turned lower shortly after opening. Stocks later rebounded, led by technology shares. Shortly after 3 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, Treasury yields hovered near session lows, with longer-term yields down as much as 5 basis points. The 2-year/10-year and 5-year/30-year spreads narrowed by 4 basis points and 1.5 basis points, respectively. The 10-year yield was down about 4 basis points at 5.07%.

The new 20-year Treasury notes were awarded at a 5.459% yield, below the record high set in October. Primary dealers received 13.1% of the auction, up from the previous sale; direct bidders received 26.7%, while indirect bidders received 60.2%. Ahead of the auction, Treasuries gained as the S&P 500 fell to a four-month low and oil prices declined. WTI crude futures settled 3.2% lower, falling below $85 a barrel for the first time since late August.

Demand for upside hedges reappeared in the Treasury options market, mainly through December-expiring 10-year Treasury 107.00 calls. Several March SOFR options structures traded actively, with positions aimed at a decline in the rate-hike premium priced into expectations for the Fed’s next several policy meetings.

As of 4:23 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, the 2-year Treasury yield was little changed at 4.8042%; the 5-year yield fell 2.7 basis points to 4.8877%; the 10-year yield fell 3.8 basis points to 5.0683%; and the 30-year yield fell 4.7 basis points to 5.411%. The 5-year/30-year spread narrowed about 2.1 basis points to 52.14 basis points, and the 2-year/10-year spread narrowed about 4.1 basis points to 26.2 basis points.

data.title: Seaport Research, Morgan Stanley Flag Nvidia Financing Shift as Risk for CoreWeave, Neoclouds
data.description: According to CNBC, CoreWeave and Iren fell around 3% in afternoon trading Wednesday, while Nebius rose around 2%, as investors anticipated tighter financing from Nvidia. The stocks’ gains after Nvidia’s earnings call on Tuesday faded. Analysts focused on changes to Nvidia’s financial footnotes, which indicate that commitments to neoclouds depend on their securing financing for data center infrastructure and may be reduced or canceled if they do not. Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia’s guarantees would begin at the specified point and would not remain in place if construction were delayed. Morgan Stanley credit analyst Lindsay Tyler kept her estimate of Nvidia’s debt adjustments and contingent obligations at around $170 billion by the end of 2028, but lowered her forecast for deployments to 4 gigawatts from 5 gigawatts. She cited neocloud commitments falling to $32 billion from $36 billion quarter over quarter. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that a half-percentage-point rate increase at the December meeting may be necessary to curb inflation.

data.title: Saifedean Ammous Says AI May Be Overvalued, Bitcoin Could Soon Rally Independently
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Bitcoin Magazine, Saifedean Ammous, author of “The Bitcoin Standard,” said on the Bitcoin Magazine T.V. (BMTV) program that Anthropic and OpenAI may ultimately be severely overvalued and questioned whether current AI valuations are justified. Ammous said Bitcoin is in a bear market but may be near the bottom, and he expects it to soon begin a rally of its own. He argued that Bitcoin and AI are not competitors, describing Bitcoin as the only thing AI cannot increase in supply. The discussion also covered fiat inflation, Federal Reserve rate hikes and debt pressures, Argentina’s inflation, stablecoins, AI capital spending, and the effects of a K-shaped economy on ordinary households.

data.title: Gomez-Bravo Sees Credit Bargains After Selloff, Calls It a Stock Picker’s Market
data.description: According to Bloomberg, MFS Investment Management’s Pilar Gomez-Bravo and J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s Iain Stealey see opportunities in beaten-up credit after the recent selloff, particularly in lower-rated and subordinated debt. Both emphasized selectivity. Gomez-Bravo called credit a “stock picker’s market,” while Stealey favored subordinated debt from strong investment-grade companies over traditional high yield. They said heavy supply and higher rates make a return to relentless spread tightening unlikely.

data.title: BTC Whale Withdraws Large Buy Order as Market Awaits Key Price Levels
data.description:
On November 18, a large BTC trader abruptly withdrew a sizable buy order in the afternoon. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, the Hyperliquid long quickly placed orders worth tens of millions of dollars at other price levels. Options implied volatility, concentrated profit-taking pressure overhead and funds waiting at lower levels are pushing BTC into a narrow trading range.

The Federal Reserve is scheduled to release minutes from its October meeting at 03:00 (UTC+8) tomorrow. At the previous meeting, some committee members voted in favor of a rate hike. After rebounding from a weekend low, Bitcoin saw U.S. spot ETFs return to net inflows for one day before flows turned negative again. Market participants are watching for key price levels as they await the minutes.

data.title: U.S. Holiday Spending Plans Top Last Year, With Growth Concentrated Among Wealthiest
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. consumers plan to spend more this holiday season than last year, but the increase is concentrated among the wealthiest households as many shoppers seek discounts and trim gift budgets.

A Conference Board survey found planned average spending on gifts and nongift items is up 5.9% from last year, or 3.2% after adjusting for inflation. Planned gift spending alone is up 2.3% after adjusting for prices. Only respondents with annual incomes of at least $200,000 plan to increase spending; their average gift budgets are 13.6% higher than in 2025. Expected gift spending is down among all other income groups.

Rising prices are squeezing many U.S. households' budgets for nonessential purchases. Larger-than-usual tax refunds and stock-market wealth effects supported consumer spending through much of this year, while wage growth largely failed to keep pace with inflation. About 38% of respondents plan to buy more promotional items, nearly 30% plan to buy fewer gifts, and 20% plan to switch to lower-priced brands or products.

The National Retail Federation reported similar findings last month, saying the top 10% of spenders will account for as much as 70% of total holiday sales as rising gasoline prices continue to pressure lower-income households.

data.title: STOCKS | Hedge Funds Add Alibaba and Futu as Stanley Druckenmiller’s Family Office Exits Baidu
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing Bloomberg, 1,191 hedge funds’ third-quarter 13F filings showed net additions of 5.5 million Alibaba ADRs, reversing two consecutive quarters of net selling. Funds also added 2.08 million Futu shares, after reducing their holdings in the previous quarter.

They cut Baidu holdings by 3.84 million shares after adding 3.5 million in the second quarter. Appaloosa LP, run by David Tepper, reduced its Baidu position, which it had increased in the prior quarter. Duquesne Family Office LLC, Stanley Druckenmiller’s family office, exited its Baidu position, opened in the previous quarter.

Other large additions included 12.06 million shares of Kanzhun, 11.68 million of JD.com and 2.54 million of PDD Holdings. Hedge funds continued adding pharmaceutical stocks, including Zai Lab and BeiGene, while reducing holdings in electric-vehicle makers such as Nio and XPeng. They also continued trimming the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (KWEB).
